summary.title_hr: Zadruge i budućnost bankarstva - Goran Jeras (ZEF i EEB)
summary.abstract_hr: Podcast istražuje nedostatke postojećeg bankarskog sustava i predstavlja zadružni model kao etičnu alternativu. Goran Jeras, upravitelj Zadruge za etično financiranje (ZEF) i CEO tvrtke ECHOES koja osniva Europsku etičnu banku (EEB), objašnjava kako komercijalne banke kreiraju novac i iscrpljuju lokalne zajednice. Razgovor naglašava demokratske principe zadruga, njihov fokus na opće dobro i planove EEB-a za financiranje priuštivog stanovanja, zelene energije i lokalnog razvoja, s ciljem zadržavanja vrijednosti unutar zajednice.
key_points: Zadruga za etično financiranje (ZEF) osnovana je prije dvanaest godina s ciljem osnivanja Hrvatske etične banke koja bi služila općem dobru i razvoju lokalne ekonomije, suprotno ekstrakcijskom bankarskom modelu.
Komercijalne banke kreiraju novac kroz kreditnu ekspanziju, stvarajući virtualni novac bez stvarne podloge, što dovodi do povećanja nejednakosti i iscrpljivanja lokalnih resursa.

Zadruge su društva osoba, a ne kapitala, funkcioniraju po demokratskom principu 'jedan član, jedan glas' i cilj im je akumulacija kapitala za zajedničku ekonomsku i društvenu infrastrukturu, zadržavajući stvorenu vrijednost u zajednici.

Primjer općine Lovinac ilustrira kako lokalna štednja završava na globalnim financijskim tržištima umjesto da se koristi za razvoj lokalne infrastrukture zbog nedostatka adekvatne financijske infrastrukture.

Kreditna politika buduće Europske etične banke (EEB) fokusirat će se na nespekulativnu proizvodnju i projekte poput priuštivog stanovanja i obnovljivih izvora energije, s ciljem podizanja kvalitete života lokalnih zajednica.

EEB će biti transparentna, javno objavljivati sve poslovne kredite i omogućiti klijentima da usmjere svoj novac prema projektima koji su u skladu s njihovim vrijednostima, nudeći fleksibilnost i inovativne usluge poput 'bank as a service'.

Koncept 'steward ownership' i Franjina ekonomija promiču ideju da poduzeća trebaju služiti općem dobru i zaštiti planeta, a ne samo profitu, što je slično zadružnom modelu i nudi put prema održivijoj ekonomiji.

key_points_en: The Cooperative for Ethical Financing (ZEF) was founded twelve years ago with the aim of establishing the Croatian Ethical Bank that would serve the common good and the development of the local economy, contrary to the extractive banking model.
Commercial banks create money through credit expansion, creating virtual money without real backing, which leads to increasing inequality and the depletion of local resources.

Cooperatives are associations of persons, not of capital, they function according to the democratic principle of 'one member, one vote' and their goal is the accumulation of capital for shared economic and social infrastructure, retaining created value in the community.

The example of the municipality of Lovinac illustrates how local savings end up on global financial markets instead of being used for the development of local infrastructure due to the lack of adequate financial infrastructure.

The credit policy of the future European Ethical Bank (EEB) will focus on non-speculative production and projects such as affordable housing and renewable energy sources, with the aim of raising the quality of life of local communities.

EEB will be transparent, publicly publishing all business loans and enabling clients to direct their money toward projects that align with their values, offering flexibility and innovative services such as 'bank as a service'.

The concept of 'steward ownership' and the Economy of Francesco promote the idea that enterprises should serve the common good and the protection of the planet, not just profit, which is similar to the cooperative model and offers a path toward a more sustainable economy.

summary.title_en: Cooperatives and the Future of Banking - Goran Jeras (ZEF and EEB)
summary.abstract_en: The podcast explores the shortcomings of the existing banking system and presents the cooperative model as an ethical alternative. Goran Jeras, manager of the Cooperative for Ethical Financing (ZEF) and CEO of the company ECHOES which is founding the European Ethical Bank (EEB), explains how commercial banks create money and deplete local communities. The conversation highlights the democratic principles of cooperatives, their focus on the common good, and the EEB's plans for financing affordable housing, green energy, and local development, with the aim of retaining value within the community.
